chunks: 3850 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who owns sheep and milks them, and they have abundant milk every day. What do you say about purchasing five hundred ritls for such-and-such dirhams, taking from it each day some ritls until he fully receives what he bought from it?
He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in this and similar transactions.”

key_terms.أَرْطَالًا: portions measured out and taken over time
key_terms.الْخَمْسِمِائَةِ رِطْلٍ: a specified measured quantity of milk being purchased
key_terms.شِرَاءِ: the act of purchase or sale agreement
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.يَسْتَوْفِيَ: to receive in full the amount purchased

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to buy a fixed amount of milk and collect it gradually each day?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a sale involving milk taken gradually over time from a flock that produces abundant milk daily. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام rules that such a transaction is permissible, indicating allowance for this type of measured deferred taking in sale.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3850 - Al-Hasan bin Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who owns sheep that produce a large quantity of milk every day.
What do you say about purchasing five hundred ritls of milk for a specified amount of dirhams, taking a certain amount from it each day until he fulfills what he purchased?
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in this and similar transactions."
